pr.body:
# Fix: Update InsightsBookingService integration tests for Prisma.sql format ## Summary This PR updates the `InsightsBookingService` integration tests to work with the new Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation. The changes follow the exact same testing patterns established in the `InsightsRoutingService` integration tests. **Key Changes:** - Replace Prisma object notation expectations with direct `Prisma.sql` template literal comparisons - Add `NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` constant for consistency with other services - Update all authorization and filter condition tests to expect raw SQL instead of object structures - Modify the final integration test to use `$queryRaw` for actual database querying - Remove complex object notation assertions in favor of direct SQL comparisons ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human ⚠️ **HIGH RISK** - This involves SQL query construction and authorization logic - [ ] **Run integration tests manually** - I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass: `TZ=UTC yarn test packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` - [ ] **Review SQL query construction** - Carefully examine the authorization conditions in the service, especially complex team/org scope logic with AND/OR combinations - [ ] **Verify authorization security** - Test with different user roles (owner, admin, member) to ensure no privilege escalation bugs - [ ] **Check parameter binding** - Ensure all user inputs in the SQL templates are properly parameterized (no injection risks) - [ ] **Test edge cases** - Verify behavior with empty teams, missing users, null values, and boundary conditions **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Run the integration tests locally to verify they pass 2. Test the service with various user roles and team configurations 3. Verify the `$queryRaw` integration test actually queries the database correctly 4. Check that authorization conditions properly restrict access based on user permissions --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD Service["packages/lib/server/service/
insightsBooking.ts"]:::context Tests["packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/
insightsBooking.integration-test.ts"]:::major-edit RoutingTests["InsightsRoutingService
integration tests
(attachment example)"]:::context Service --> Tests RoutingTests --> Tests Tests --> AuthTests["Authorization Condition Tests
- NOTHING_CONDITION
- User/Team/Org scope"]:::major-edit Tests --> FilterTests["Filter Condition Tests
- Event type filtering
- Member user filtering"]:::major-edit Tests --> IntegrationTest["Database Integration Test
- $queryRaw usage
- Real query execution"]:::major-edit subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - This conversion was based on the InsightsRoutingService integration test patterns provided in the user's attachment - The test runner had configuration issues during development, so manual verification of test execution is critical - All test expectations now use direct `Prisma.sql` comparisons instead of inspecting `.strings` and `.values` properties - The NOTHING_CONDITION constant ensures consistency across different insight services **Session Info:** Requested by @eunjae-lee | Session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a5e216ec6c364679a220f799e2abc700

raw_findings.body: SQL operator precedence applies the caller's additional predicate only to the final OR branch, so authorized team bookings that do not satisfy the requested date, status, or other filter are still returned.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A query shaped as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND extra_condition` is evaluated as `team_branch OR (user_branch AND extra_condition)` instead of `(team_branch OR user_branch) AND extra_condition`.
raw_findings.impact: SQL operator precedence applies the caller's additional predicate only to the final OR branch, so authorized team bookings that do not satisfy the requested date, status, or other filter are still returned.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new composable SQL API returns a top-level OR authorization fragment unchanged when no service filter is present.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap this branch before returning it, for example `return Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`;`, or ensure every authorization builder returns one outer-parenthesized predicate.
raw_findings.title: Parenthesize authorization OR expressions before returning them as a base predicate
raw_findings.trigger: A team- or organization-scoped service has no filters, its authorization condition contains both team-booking and user-booking OR branches, and a caller embeds `getBaseConditions()` next to another `AND` predicate such as a date or status restriction.

raw_findings.body: TypeScript consumers no longer compile, while untyped consumers fail at runtime with `findMany is not a function`; caller-provided selection and where arguments also have no compatible replacement.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Method lookup or compilation fails before the booking query can execute.
raw_findings.impact: TypeScript consumers no longer compile, while untyped consumers fail at runtime with `findMany is not a function`; caller-provided selection and where arguments also have no compatible replacement.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch deletes the public `findMany` method while introducing a differently shaped `getBaseConditions` API without a compatibility layer.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Retain a compatibility method or migrate every consumer to a documented replacement before removing it; if this is an intentionally breaking public change, expose it through an explicit versioned migration rather than silently replacing the method.
raw_findings.title: Removing findMany breaks the exported service API
raw_findings.trigger: An existing TypeScript or JavaScript consumer of the exported `InsightsBookingService` invokes its previously public `findMany` method.

raw_findings.body: The invalid request now passes compile-time checking, is rejected only by `safeParse`, and silently produces the `1=0` authorization condition and empty insights rather than identifying the missing team identifier at the call site.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Static validation accepts an impossible team-scope state that runtime validation converts into a fail-closed but misleading empty result.
raw_findings.impact: The invalid request now passes compile-time checking, is rejected only by `safeParse`, and silently produces the `1=0` authorization condition and empty insights rather than identifying the missing team identifier at the call site.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly duplicated public options type replaces the schema-derived discriminated union with one broad shape whose `teamId` is always optional.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (or `z.input<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>`) as the constructor type, preserving the discriminated union where `teamId` is mandatory only for `scope: "team"`.
raw_findings.title: Keep constructor options discriminated so teamId remains required for team scope
raw_findings.trigger: A TypeScript caller constructs options such as `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without a `teamId`.

raw_findings.body: The integration suite can pass by comparing `Prisma.Sql` object structure even though those authorization fragments fail against PostgreSQL or return incorrectly filtered rows in production.
raw_findings.evidence: const results = await prisma.$queryRaw<{ id: number }[]>`
raw_findings.failure_mode: SQL binding, syntax, precedence, and result-semantic regressions in the highest-risk authorization paths are not exercised by the test database.
raw_findings.impact: The integration suite can pass by comparing `Prisma.Sql` object structure even though those authorization fragments fail against PostgreSQL or return incorrectly filtered rows in production.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch converts authorization to executable raw SQL but only executes the scalar user-scope path; the array and OR branches are asserted structurally.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add raw-query integration cases for both team and organization scopes, including populated user-ID arrays, an empty-membership branch, and an additional `AND` predicate with no service filters to verify grouping and actual result sets.
raw_findings.title: Execute the team and organization SQL branches in integration tests
raw_findings.trigger: The newly generated team- or organization-scope SQL uses array-valued `ANY` parameters, OR composition, or no-filter composition incorrectly while the sole raw-query test continues to exercise only user scope with scalar parameters.

finding.trigger: A TypeScript caller constructs options such as `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without a `teamId`.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (lines 29-34) with optional teamId, while the schema requires teamId for scope:'team'. The constructor accepts InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (line 58), allowing TypeScript callers to pass {scope:'team', userId, orgId} without teamId. Runtime safeParse catches this but returns null options, leading to NOTHING_CONDITION silently. This weakens compile-time safety for the team scope case.
